fieldValues.title: Keeping SVG images free of scripts
fieldValues.decision_question: How is an SVG image kept from running scripts?
fieldValues.context: The owner, 2026-11-08 (vignette 02e02668): 'Lets support svgs without scripts.' An SVG is XML and can carry
fieldValues.friction: A hostile SVG attached to a shared essay could run in a reader's browser if any surface ever shows it inline.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: A. Two layers (recommended): the core refuses an unsafe SVG when it is attached (error code svg-unsafe), and every client shows images only through an element from a blob URL, never inline SVG or HTML injection. For: defence in depth; the core check protects every client and the CLI. Against: two things to build and test. B. Client display rule only. For: smallest. Against: unsafe files still enter repositories and reach other clients. C. Rewrite SVGs to strip scripts. For: accepts more files. Against: rewriting the writer's file changes it silently; sanitisers have a long bug history. D. No SVG. Against: the owner's ruling.
fieldValues.key_requirements: No script ever runs (owner); the writer's file is never rewritten; one rule for every client.
fieldValues.decision_statement: An SVG with a script, an event attribute, foreign content or an external reference is refused when attached, and clients show SVG images only as image elements.
fieldValues.rationale: Refusing is clearer than rewriting, and the display rule closes the gap if a refusal is ever missed.
fieldValues.revisit_when: Writers' ordinary diagram tools produce SVGs that the check refuses, or a client needs inline SVG for interaction.
